glossary.regime: How the model describes the market now: rising, falling, moving sideways or experiencing unusually large moves.
glossary.probabilityUp: The model's estimate of the chance that the market rises over the selected period.
glossary.volatility: How sharply prices move up and down. Higher volatility usually means greater short-term risk.
glossary.riskState: A composite assessment of current risk based on volatility, drawdown and market state.
glossary.forecastInterval: A range of possible outcomes. A wider range means the model is less certain.
glossary.drawdown: The fall from the most recent peak. A 10% drawdown means the value is 10% below that peak.
glossary.var: Value at Risk (VaR) is an estimated loss threshold under normal conditions. It is not the largest possible loss.
glossary.es: Expected Shortfall is the average loss in cases that are worse than the VaR threshold.
glossary.sharpe: Excess return per unit of total risk. Higher is better.
glossary.sortino: Like Sharpe, but only penalizes downside volatility.
glossary.calmar: Annualized return divided by maximum drawdown.
glossary.profitFactor: Gross profit divided by gross loss. Above 1 means net profitable.
glossary.winRate: The share of trades that were profitable.
glossary.turnover: How actively the portfolio trades. More turnover means more cost.
glossary.exposure: The share of time the system holds a market position.
glossary.basis: The spread between the futures price and the underlying index.
glossary.coverage: The share of actual outcomes that fell inside the forecast range. It shows whether that range was reliable.
glossary.monteCarlo: Monte Carlo simulation creates many possible scenarios to estimate the range of outcomes and risks.
glossary.bootstrap: Repeatedly resampling past data to check whether a result is stable or may have occurred by chance.
glossary.downsideProbability: The estimated probability of a negative return over the evaluation horizon.
glossary.modelConsensus: The degree of agreement between independent models on the current market state.

about.title: About us
about.lead: Quant Percent is a quantitative research group working on the Vietnamese market. We build models, test them on data they have never seen, and publish the ones that do not work alongside the ones that do. Most quantitative research does not survive contact with new data — we think that should be said out loud rather than hidden.
about.whatText:
A quantitative research group. We take no capital, run no portfolios for anyone else, and sell no buy-or-sell recommendations.

What we produce is models, testing methodology, and public reports carrying enough data for a reader to judge the work themselves instead of taking our word for it.
about.publishText:
Every report states the data period, the testing method, and the full set of performance and risk figures. Results are broken out by period, including the losing ones.

Where the data is not enough to conclude something, we say it is not enough rather than filling in a plausible-looking number.

founder.name: Phạm Minh Huy
founder.bio: The question that has followed me from the first day is still the same: why trust an indicator you do not understand? It is what brought me to mathematics and data — not to predict the market, but to understand it. And I believe every investor, institutional or individual, deserves that lens: the one that lets them see past the numbers on the surface to the real shape of the market moving underneath.

about.philosophyText:
A forecast is never certain, return always travels with risk, and every model has a stretch where it performs badly.

Every conclusion on this site states where the data came from, which period it was tested over, and what its limits are. A result without those three is not ready to publish.
about.focusText:
We concentrate on the VN-Index, stocks listed on HOSE, and the VN30F1M futures contract.

The narrow scope is deliberate: it lets data collection, model construction and validation stay consistent, rather than covering everything and going shallow everywhere.
about.stageText:
Quant Percent is at the research and validation stage. Four models have completed an independent, time-ordered testing cycle, the data system runs daily across every stock listed on HOSE, and Model Modus has been through three years of validation.

The next step is supervised operation: running the models in real time and comparing live results against the tested ones, for long enough to know how far apart the two are.
developingItems: Index and stock forecasts across multiple time frames
Rule-based trading systems for the derivatives market
Data infrastructure and model quality monitoring
about.note: Quant Percent does not currently operate a formal capital management business and does not raise or accept discretionary funds through this website.
about.ctaText: We talk to research groups, data partners, and quantitative practitioners with an interest in the Vietnamese market.

legal.title: Legal
legal.intro: Please read the following terms carefully before using content on the Quant Percent website.

items.title: Nature of content
items.text: Quant Percent is currently a quantitative research group. Content on this website is provided for informational and research purposes only and does not constitute personalized investment advice, an offer to invest, or any guarantee of returns.

items.title: Forecast uncertainty
items.text: All forecasts carry uncertainty. Forecast intervals and probabilities are statistical estimates, not commitments about outcomes.

items.title: Past results
items.text: Past results, including backtests and paper trading, do not guarantee future outcomes.

items.title: Backtest limitations
items.text: Backtests are built on historical data and may be affected by overfitting, selection bias and execution assumptions.

items.title: Paper trading
items.text: Paper trading is simulated operation and differs from live trading in execution, liquidity, costs and psychology.

items.title: Data delays and revisions
items.text: Displayed data may lag real time and may be revised as data sources update.

items.title: Model changes
items.text: Models are under continuous research and may change, be paused or be removed without notice.

items.title: User responsibility
items.text: Users are solely responsible for their own investment decisions. Trading securities and derivatives carries risk of capital loss.

items.title: No substitute for professional advice
items.text: Information on this website does not replace investment, legal or tax advice from licensed professionals.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy describes how Quant Percent collects, uses and protects your personal data when you use this website.

sections.title: Data we collect
sections.text: When you submit the contact form, we collect your name, email, phone and organization (if provided), inquiry type and message. When you create an account, we store your name, email and a hashed password.

sections.title: The portfolio you enter
sections.text: The portfolio tool computes on the tickers, quantities, cash and loan you enter. This data is sent only to be computed and then discarded, never written to the database — unless you press "Save portfolio"; only what you entered is then stored under your account — never the analysis. A saved portfolio is visible only to you, can be deleted at any time, and is deleted with the account.

sections.title: How we use it
sections.text: Contact data is used only to respond to your inquiry and, if you registered interest, to inform you about future research and partnership opportunities. We do not sell or share your data with third parties for advertising.

sections.title: Storage and protection
sections.text: Data is stored with access control and processed only by responsible personnel. We apply reasonable technical measures against unauthorized access.

sections.title: Retention
sections.text: Contact data is retained for as long as needed to handle your inquiry and at most 24 months after the last contact, unless the law requires otherwise.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.text: You may request access to, correction of, or deletion of your personal data by contacting us through the website form.

sections.title: Cookies
sections.text: This website uses only technical cookies necessary for operation (such as remembering your language). No advertising or third-party tracking cookies are used.

result.forwardLead: This takes the simulated VN-Index distribution ({paths} scenarios, {baseDays} sessions each) and carries it across to the portfolio: scaled by a beta of {beta} for how closely the book tracks the index, then stretched by square-root-of-time to answer for the {horizonDays} sessions you picked. result.forwardCaveat: This is an indirect estimate. It carries the index's risk across by beta, so it does not capture risk specific to the individual holdings, and the square-root-of-time stretch ignores both drift and volatility clustering — the further from the {baseDays}-session simulation, the looser it gets. A simulated probability is not a certainty.
result.glossaryLead: Explained using the portfolio just entered.

explain.var95: About one trading day in 20 is a bad day. On that day the portfolio usually loses {pct} or more, roughly {amount}. It marks where bad days begin, not the worst possible loss.
explain.es95: The "bad day" figure only says where bad days begin, not how deep they go. "Very bad day" is the average loss on those bad days: about {pct}, roughly {amount}.
explain.maxDrawdown: Had this portfolio been held throughout the measured period, its value at one point stood {pct} below the peak previously reached, around {amount}. This is a recorded decline, not an estimate.
explain.riskContribution: Share of capital is the money allocated to a holding. Share of risk is that holding's responsibility for the movement of the whole portfolio, depending both on its own volatility and on how closely it moves with the others. A holding representing a quarter of capital can contribute more than half of total risk.
explain.effectiveBets: The portfolio holds {positions} stocks, but if they move together then in risk terms the diversification achieved is equivalent to fewer holdings. Accounting for this, the portfolio is equivalent to about {bets} independent positions.
explain.beta: A beta of {beta} means that when VN-Index moves 10%, this portfolio typically moves about {move} in the same direction. Above 1 is more sensitive than the market, below 1 less.
explain.betaMissing: Not enough index data on the same dates as the portfolio to compute this.
explain.correlation: The figure {value} is the average correlation across every pair of stocks in the portfolio. Closer to 1 means the holdings move together and diversification is less effective; closer to 0 means they are more independent.

result.exceedanceNote: The deeper the decline, the lower its probability. A point above the 50% line is more likely to occur than not. The horizontal axis is fixed, so two portfolios — or one portfolio at two periods — can be read against the same scale.
result.lossScaleNote: The same decline levels, valued against the stocks held. Cash is excluded.
result.closestPairHigh: almost one position — they fall together
result.closestPairLow: move together little — they complement each other
result.volatilityNote: over a year the portfolio usually swings up and down within this range
result.varCheckShort: days that lost more than it ({rate}); about 5% is normal
result.histNote: Each column is the number of days the portfolio gained or lost that much. The red area is the worst days — about 1 day in 20.
result.lossTip2: A "bad day" is the loss you meet about once every 20 trading days. A "very bad day" is the average loss on those bad days.
result.badDayNote: about one day in 20 loses this much or more ({pct})
result.veryBadDayNote: the average loss on those bad days ({pct})

margin.heading: Capital structure and margin
margin.lead: The same portfolio, seen from your own money rather than from the stocks. Every figure is arithmetic on the loan you entered and the measures above; this section does not say how much to borrow.

status.between: The margin ratio of {ratio} is below the warning threshold of {call} and above the forced-sale threshold of {force}. If the figures are right, the broker has already asked for more collateral; if you have not been asked, check the loan and the positions entered.
status.below_force: The margin ratio of {ratio} is below the forced-sale threshold of {force}. An account at this level has usually already been sold down by the broker — or the figures are wrong. The numbers below only mean something if the figures are right.
status.negative_equity: The loan of {debt} exceeds total assets of {assets}: equity is negative. With brokerage margin this cannot happen — check for an extra zero, or positions in the account not yet entered. If the loan is from outside the brokerage, tick "not brokerage margin".

margin.ratioNote: The simple form: equity over total assets. Brokers compute it on collateral discounted stock by stock, so your real ratio is lower and the thresholds closer than shown here.
margin.distanceNote: a further {amount} fall in the stocks; forced sale at −{force}
margin.idleCashNote: per year, because {cash} of cash sits next to a loan that is charging interest
margin.idleCashNone: no cash held alongside the loan
margin.horizonTitle: The same loan, held for how long?
margin.horizonNote: Two independent estimates of the stocks falling to the warning threshold within the period: the Certus simulation scaled to the portfolio by beta, and how often VN-Index has fallen that far within a window this long since 2000. Interest and break-even are arithmetic.
margin.horizonNoteNoBeta: The portfolio does not track the index closely enough to scale a probability from VN-Index, so only the interest cost is shown. Break-even is the rise the stocks need just to cover the interest.
margin.historyNote: The historical frequency counts {windows} rolling VN-Index windows since 2000, scaled to the portfolio by beta. A short period is only low-probability on average: in March 2020 the index lost a third in six weeks.
margin.scenarioNote: Cash and the loan stay as they are. The last column is the cash that brings the margin ratio back to the warning threshold — the same arithmetic the broker's app shows, not a recommendation.
margin.equityRiskNote: The same three figures as in "Losses the portfolio may take", turned into money and set against your equity. The grey bar is the loss without a loan; the red bar is that loss divided by your own money — longer by exactly the leverage. Reaching the black line means all equity is gone.

caveat.selfReported: Computed from the loan, rate and thresholds you entered, at the latest close. Nothing is verified with the broker.
caveat.collateral: Brokers compute the margin ratio on collateral discounted per stock; every distance here is an optimistic estimate.
caveat.model: The simulated probability inherits every limit of the "Chance of a decline ahead" section: the 1-year row stretches a 20-session simulation by ×3.5.
caveat.rollover: Margin loans usually run for about three months and are rolled over; at rollover the broker may change loan ratios or drop a stock from the margin list. That risk is not in any figure above.

warnings.debt_exceeds_stocks: The loan of {debt} exceeds the stock value of {stocks}. A broker does not lend beyond the collateral — possibly an extra zero, positions not yet entered, or a loan from outside the brokerage (tick the box in the form).
warnings.high_leverage: Leverage of {leverage}× — above what brokerage margin normally allows (about 2×). If correct, most of the assets are borrowed.
warnings.rate_unusual: A rate of {rate} per year is outside the usual 5–25% range for margin in Vietnam. Check the unit (%/year).

margin.horizonNoteExternal: An external loan has no warning threshold, so only the interest cost is shown. Break-even is the rise the stocks need just to cover the interest.
margin.horizonNotePast: The account is already below the warning threshold, so the "chance of reaching it" is moot and not shown. Only the interest cost by holding period remains.
margin.equityLegendAll: Black line: all of your equity ({amount})
margin.scenarioExternal: An external loan has no brokerage threshold, so there is no forced-sale scenario.
margin.dumbbellNote: The red dot sits {leverage}× further than the grey one — the leverage.

saved.heading: Saved portfolios
saved.done: Saved. Next time you sign in, open it from the list above.
saved.note: Only the inputs are saved, not the result. {remaining} left.
saved.limit: You have saved the maximum of 10 portfolios. Delete an old one to save another.

network.heading: Your holdings on the VN30 dependency map
network.lead: DynamicGraph measures which stocks move together once the market's common swing is removed, and groups them into communities. Your holdings are highlighted; the rest of VN30 is faded. Several holdings in one community means they answer to the same factor — diversified on paper, not in practice.
network.source: Network estimated on the last {window} sessions. This is the model's descriptive layer, validated as stable from session to session; it is not a price forecast.

stressLabel.high_stress: tight links — stocks are moving together more than usual

network.uncovered: The map covers VN30 only. {symbols} ({share} of the portfolio) are outside it and not drawn.
network.allCovered: Every holding is in VN30 and appears on the map.

outlook.heading: Return range from the Causa model
outlook.lead: Causa forecasts the distribution of VN-Index returns over 5, 20 and 60 sessions. Each column is the range holding {level} of outcomes according to the model, scaled to the portfolio by beta {beta} — and onto equity when there is a loan. No centre line is drawn: the model's own report says its point forecast has not beaten a baseline; only the range is validated.
outlook.source: The model runs on VN-Index; scaling to the portfolio by beta ignores each stock's own risk.
outlook.caveat: The interest line is the rise the stocks need to pay the interest over that period; the warning line is the fall that reaches the warning threshold. Both are arithmetic, not forecasts.
outlook.compareLead: The same {level} Causa interval per horizon: grey box is VN-Index, blue box is the portfolio scaled by beta {beta}. A wider blue box means the portfolio swings more than the market.

stress.heading: If a crisis came back
stress.lead: This portfolio, at today's weights, run through the prices of the largest falls since 2008: how deep it would have fallen, against VN-Index over the same sessions. No assumptions — this is what happened to the stocks you hold.
stress.coverageNote: Holdings not yet listed at the time are left out and the rest re-weighted; the last column says how much of the portfolio each replay covers.
stress.equityNote: The "on equity" column multiplies the fall by today's leverage; "reaches warning" compares that fall with the distance to the broker's threshold.
stress.liquidityNote: Time to sell assumes only {share} of a stock's normal daily volume is sold per day, so the sale itself does not push the price down.
stress.noCrises: Too few holdings were listed through past falls to replay them.
stress.noDiv: If every holding fell at once
stress.noDivNote: annual volatility would rise to this instead of {now} — when diversification stops helping
stress.liquidity: If you had to sell everything, how long?
stress.liquiditySlow: {symbols} ({share} of the portfolio) need about {days} sessions to sell — a forced sale gets prices well below the board.
stress.liquidityFine: Every holding can be exited at once: what you hold is small next to its daily volume.
stress.pickHint: Pick a period above to watch your portfolio go through it — pick more to compare.

budget.heading: The loss you would accept
budget.lead: Your limit, on {basis}, set against the deepest fall the portfolio went through over the last year and through the crisis replays above. The page does not say what to change to fit inside it — that is your decision.
budget.probabilityNote: The chance of reaching the limit comes from the Certus simulation scaled to the portfolio by beta, next to how often VN-Index has fallen that far over the same horizon since 2000.
budget.limitNote: {pct} of {basis}; a {drop} fall in the stocks reaches it
budget.probabilityNone: the portfolio does not track the index closely enough to estimate
budget.probabilityModelOnly: Certus simulation scaled to the portfolio
budget.probabilityWithHistory: Certus simulation; VN-Index history since 2000: {history} of windows this long
